title: Kinds of Galaxies
objective: After this level you can tell spiral, elliptical and irregular galaxies apart.
summary: Galaxies come in three main shapes: spirals with arms and new stars, smooth ellipticals of old stars, and shapeless irregulars.

cards.headline: Galaxies come in shapes, and each shape tells a story.
Three main types
cards.body: In the 1920s Edwin Hubble sorted galaxies by shape. Spiral galaxies have a flat, rotating disk with spiral arms, where young stars are still forming. Elliptical galaxies are smooth, rounded collections of mostly older stars, with little new star formation.

cards.headline: And the rest
cards.body: Irregular galaxies have no clear shape at all. Two of the best known, the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds, are close neighbors of the Milky Way.

cards.fact: Our galaxy is a barred spiral.
cards.context: The Milky Way is a spiral with a bar of stars across its center, as you first learned back in Level 1.

cards.headline: Galaxy types: sorted
learned: Galaxies are spiral, elliptical or irregular
Spirals have arms full of young stars
Ellipticals are smooth and mostly old

questions.prompt: Which kind of galaxy has a flat, rotating disk with arms winding out from its center?

options.label: Globular
options.rationale: Globular clusters are star clusters, not galaxy types.

questions.explanation: Spiral galaxies have flat, rotating disks with spiral arms.

questions.prompt: An astronomer finds a galaxy of mostly old stars with little new star formation. What type is it most likely?

options.label: Spiral
options.rationale: Spirals are still forming young stars in their arms.

options.label: Barred spiral
options.rationale: Barred spirals also form stars in their arms.

questions.explanation: Elliptical galaxies are smooth collections of mostly older stars with little ongoing star formation.

questions.prompt: From Level 66: where in a spiral galaxy would you expect to find the most stellar nurseries?

options.label: In the halo around the galaxy
Only at the exact center
options.rationale: Most star formation is in the disk.

options.label: Nowhere: spirals no longer form stars

questions.explanation: Spiral arms are rich in gas and dust, where new stars are forming.
